subject: Clarify billing cadence for hybrid long-context sessions and discount ask
raw_messages:
From: Gina Lopez <gina.lopez@greenleaf.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenleaf.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence question for hybrid sessions + discount request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we're excited about Redwood's hybrid routing and the KV cache improvements. Before we move the SOW to procurement, there are two open items we need firm answers on from billing:

1) How do you meter "hybrid" sessions that combine short interactive calls and long-context streaming? In our pilot we see many sessions that are ~30s of streaming + a 6k-token follow-up. Do you charge per API call, per token, or is there an aggregation window?

2) Rounding: when you round up, what's the smallest quantum? Our finance team prefers predictability; if you're rounding per-call to 1k tokens that materially inflates spend for us. Can you share sample math for 1 week of traffic?

Separately, GreenLeaf is prepared to commit $50k/mo for a 12-month commit if we can get a 20-25% discount and a mechanism to smooth over bursty weeks (so we don't pay full rounding penalties on low-utilization tails). Is that a conversation you can have pricing own?

I've attached our current usage dump (billing-examples.csv) so you can see distribution.

Appreciate a quick confirm or call — procurement is looking to finalize by end of week.

Best,
Gina Lopez
Director, Platform Integrations
GreenLeaf Health

---

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 10:40 AM -0700 Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Gina Lopez <gina.lopez@greenleaf.com>
Cc: procurement@greenleaf.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question for hybrid sessions + discount request

Hi Gina — thanks for the file and for being explicit about the commitment. Short answers up front, longer below:

- Metering: we meter at the token level; however, we apply a configurable aggregation window by customer that lets us aggregate multiple API calls from the same session into a single billing unit for the purposes of rounding.
- Rounding quantum: default platform quantum is 100 tokens per-charge; for committed customers we can change that to 50 tokens or do monthly smoothing so the per-call rounding doesn’t inflate spend.

Below is a worked example using your CSV (simplified):
- Week sample: 1,200 API calls; median call size 320 tokens; 150 long-context operations averaging 6,200 tokens; streaming segments average 700 tokens (most are followed by the long op).
- If billed per-call with 100-token quantum and no smoothing: rounded_total = sum(ceil(call_tokens/100) * 100) -> shows ~8% uplift vs raw token count.
- If we aggregate calls within a 10-minute window per session before rounding: uplift drops to ~1.7%.
- If we reduce quantum to 50 tokens + monthly smoothing: uplift becomes negligible (~0.6%).

For discounting: pricing can work a few ways — a straight % off list for a committed spend, or a two-tier model where we promise a commit and provide a carryover credit for unused committed tokens to smooth month-to-month rounding pains.

I'll loop Ben for the discount framing and legal/ops constraints. Can you confirm whether the long-context ops are coming from the same session IDs (i.e., is the 30s streaming and the 6k follow-up in the same session)? If so, session-level aggregation will give you the biggest win.

Cheers,
Irene
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 17, 2026 at 08:15 AM -0700 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Gina Lopez <gina.lopez@greenleaf.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question for hybrid sessions + discount request

Gina — thanks for the examples and for the clarity on commit size. A few commercial options we can offer GreenLeaf: 

1) Commitment discount (recommended): 15% off list in exchange for $50k/mo 12-month commit. Includes monthly smoothing credits (unused committed spend becomes a credit, expires after 3 months) and reduction of quantum to 50 tokens for the account. This keeps us predictable and addresses your rounding concerns.

2) Usage + buffer model: 10% off list, no carryover credits, but we apply a 5k token monthly buffer that absorbs rounding uplift for low-volume tails. Simpler but less favorable to you long-term.

3) Pilot carve-out (short-term): 20% off for the first 3 months while we validate session-level aggregation and KV-cache savings; revert to 12% after pilot unless commit executed. Good if procurement needs a shorter runway.

Operational notes: session-level aggregation requires you to pass a session_id header consistently — our SDK supports this. Streaming partial charges: we bill tokens as they are emitted but aggregation can happen in near-real time (10s windows) for rounding. For auditability we can produce an hourly token-rollup export so your finance team can reconcile rounding deltas.

If you want the 20-25% you mentioned, we can do that limited to pilots or with an extended commitment (18-24mo) and a higher minimum commit.

Next step suggestion: a 30-minute call Wednesday to choose between option 1 vs pilot. I'll prepare sample invoice math using your CSV so you can show procurement the delta.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: billing-examples.csv (usage sample)
